calls.title: [EXTERNO]: Re: [EXTERNO]: Re: [EXTERNO]: Re: GrowthBook proposal
calls.summary: The team is working to finalize a user-based contract with a yearly price structure that includes a fixed fee plus per-user costs, aiming for completion by July 31. The contractual agreement encompasses a yearly fee of around $40,000 for 110 users, which features a discounted user price negotiated down from $1,250 to $650. The procurement process requires legal review of the order form and includes a timely structured approach for supplier onboarding and issuance of a purchase order. Budget constraints were discussed, noting a $20,000 shortfall, and the flexibility of user count was highlighted to fit budget considerations. The pilot program successfully transitioned from proof of concept to production-level tests, showcasing effective vendor engagement. Coordinating internal stakeholders is crucial as Pedro leads this effort amid team transitions.
calls.keywords: POC, Contract negotiation, User licensing, Budget constraints, Vendor management, Purchase Order

calls.summary: The team decided to proceed with contract signing via DocuSign to streamline the process and avoid project delays. Ryan confirmed that only his signature is needed at this stage, which allows the business to advance without waiting for multiple signatures. Legal concerns regarding the Data Processing Agreement (DPA) and privacy notice will be handled separately, with Ryan confirming the order form can be signed while these details are reviewed later. This pragmatic approach balances risk management and operational speed. Additionally, a minor issue with the residence certificate document was identified, which will be addressed via email, ensuring clarity without impacting the contract progress.
calls.keywords: Assignment, DocuSign, Signature, Data Processing Agreement, Privacy Notice, Residence Certificate
